_comment: Generated by scripts/vr-gen-federal-wave-f7-vote-seed.mjs. Do not hand-edit; regenerate.
source: senate.gov LIS roll-call XML (14) and clerk.house.gov EVS XML (5), read live and cached under $F7_XML_DIR

attribution.house: fail-closed: the clerk's own name-id (bioguide) → db/vr-member-map.json → roster slug, and no other path
attribution.senate: fail-closed: (surname, state) against the roster's whole name, because Senate XML carries no bioguide. A surname matching two distinct roster people is skipped and counted as ambiguous, never split by guess.
attribution.tallyAuthority: Senate <count><yeas>/<nays>; House <totals-by-vote>. Never the LIS <vote_tally> display string, which renders '51-42' and parses as 5142.
attribution.unresolvedArePart: Members who do not resolve are skipped and counted per roll in _unresolvedRecorded and _ambiguousSkipped, so the ceiling is visible rather than implied.

votes.question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 83
votes.voteDesc: Motion to Discharge S. J. Res. 83 from the Committee on Foreign Relations
votes.decisiveWhy: A war-powers resolution under 50 U.S.C. 1544(c) reaches the floor only if the Foreign Relations Committee is discharged, so the discharge motion IS the vote on the resolution: a rejected motion ends the measure and no vote on passage ever occurs. This is the same admitted form F4 used for the arms-sale disapprovals.

votes.question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 98
votes.decisiveWhy: A war-powers resolution under 50 U.S.C. 1544(c) reaches the floor only if the Foreign Relations Committee is discharged, and this is that motion. Unlike the twelve rejected motions in this wave it CARRIED, so it did not by itself end the measure — and the sentence is written out rather than borrowed, because the borrowed one would be false here. No vote on passage followed: the resolution fell on 119/2/9 when a point of order against it was sustained, 50-50. That roll is a form rule 8/12 does not admit, so the discharge motion remains the only recorded position on the merits of this text, and it is the roll admitted. The resolution did not pass the Senate.

declinedFacets.why: Read and withheld, not read and rejected: restraint fits this text exactly as it fits the four Iran resolutions this wave DID map, which is the whole problem. Eleven Iran withdrawal resolutions reached a discharge vote in this Congress on the same operative command, and mapping all eleven would file one subject eleven times and let a member's roll 119/2/58 ballot be counted again as a separate judgment. Runbook rule 34 admits a repeat only where the roll is the only record of somebody's position, and every senator recorded on S.J.Res. 118 is also recorded on a mapped sibling. The roll is ingested in full; what is withheld is the mapping.

Withheld for the same reason as the restraint row, and with less lost: war_powers sits in _RD_NO_POLE, so the row would have printed no direction in any case. It would still have added weight to a member's judged-act count on a question their mapped Iran rolls already record, which is double-counting by another name. Ingested, attributed and citable at roll 119/2/58; unmapped on purpose.

Withheld. The opposed reading is as real here as on the mapped Iran resolutions, and that is precisely why it may not be filed seven more times: strong_defense is a chip a reader compares across a whole file, and seven extra rows on one repeated question would move a member's reading on defence posture without a single new position behind it. The vote is on file at roll 119/2/58 and reads to nobody.
